item.title: Michigan court overturns $1.55 million judgment against couple who backed out of home purchase
item.description: In an intriguing legal twist, a Michigan appeals court has vacated a $1.55 million judgment against a couple who pulled out of purchasing a home over unresolved ownership concerns. The court uncovered notable procedural errors in the trial, chiefly concerning jury instructions and discussions deemed confidential. Consequently, the previous damages assessment was overturned, and the case is now set to return to the trial court.

item.title: Australian court upholds A$99,382 award over neighbour's blocked drain flooding backyard and pool
item.description: In a significant legal victory, an Australian homeowner triumphed over his neighbor who contributed to ongoing flooding that devastated his land and pool. The New South Wales Court of Appeal upheld the initial ruling, assigning liability to the uphill property owners for inadequate drainage. They were ordered to compensate A$99,382.01 and to execute necessary repairs to avert further flooding.

item.title: Irish farmer builds solar farm on 1.5 acres, powers 150 homes while sheep graze beneath panels
item.description: In County Cork, Sean Keating, a dedicated dairy farmer, has innovatively transformed a portion of his land into a solar farm. This eco-friendly venture enables him to harvest renewable energy while still allowing sheep to graze comfortably beneath the solar installations. Expected to power about 150 households annually, this project showcases the critical support from the government and could potentially motivate other farmers to explore similar sustainable energy alternatives.

item.title: Shay Mitchell sells renovated 1931 Los Angeles home for $1.95 million, three years after buying it
item.description: Shay Mitchell has made waves once again as she sells her stunning Los Angeles home for $1.95 million. Originally bought in 2012 for $1.35 million, this vintage property boasts traditional Spanish architecture, enhanced by modern upgrades that made it highly appealing. The flourishing real estate market of spring 2015 contributed to its quick sale, paving the way for the actress to invest in a larger estate in the area.

item.title: Forgotten attic jewellery collection fetches £506,750 at auction, including rare 1905 Cartier brooch
item.description: A long-hidden jewellery collection from Worcestershire unexpectedly fetched £506,750 at auction, surpassing the initial estimate of £150,000. This remarkable sale featured over 200 items, captivating global bidders. Among them, a rare brooch and necklace attracted particularly fierce competition, reflecting their exceptional quality. Profits from this auction will be distributed among the heirs of the deceased owner, marking a remarkable conclusion to a decades-long enigma.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Free High-Tech Halloween Show: Long Beach couple sync 28-computer display; families flock for community magic
item.description: Every year, Jeff and Ann Haberman delight Long Beach with their spectacular Halloween display, enchanting families with synchronized lights, music, and lively animations. The elaborate setup is managed by 28 computers, enhancing the overall experience through striking visual effects and projections. Upholding their festive tradition, they will launch a Christmas display on December 1, while also contributing to children's mental health services through their fundraising initiatives.
item.dc:creator: TOI Lifestyle Desk

item.title: Colin Farrell’s foundation selects 16 US organisations for grants supporting adults with disabilities
item.description: With a commitment to enhancing the lives of individuals with intellectual and developmental disabilities, the Colin Farrell Foundation has launched multiple grant initiatives across the country. By selecting 16 key organizations, the foundation focuses on fostering improved housing and employment options. These initiatives are crafted to enhance community engagement and address essential service gaps as young adults transition to independent living, creating a strong support system for their families.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: California vineyard estate sells for $11.04 million
item.description: A vineyard estate in Portola Valley sold for $11.04 million, which was initially listed for $15.5 million. This property included a three-level Italian villa overlooking San Francisco Bay, featuring six bedrooms and nine bathrooms. The estate had several luxury amenities, including a theatre, a spa, and outdoor entertainment areas. The estate belonged to the Fogarty Family Trust, linked to Dr. Thomas J. Fogarty, the winery founder.
item.dc:creator: TOI Real Estate Desk

item.title: Denver Parkland Protections Advance: City taps MVVA for Park Hill design; bond funds back new park
item.description: Denver is advancing plans to convert the former Park Hill Golf Course into Park Hill Park. The city has selected Michael Van Valkenburgh Associates to design the 155-acre site. Voters rejected a development proposal for the land in 2023, emphasizing its importance as public space. Funding for the project includes $70 million approved through the Vibrant Denver Bond program.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Rare Edvard Munch print bought in 1969 resurfaces in England, valued at up to £80,000
item.description: On 28 October 2026, Catherine Southon Auctioneers will present an extraordinary woodcut print by Edvard Munch, previously in the possession of a prominent Norwegian family. Titled Melancholy III, this artwork carries an estimated auction price of £50,000 to £80,000, spotlighting its cultural significance. The included sales receipt from Norway, dated back to 1969, provides a rich context, showcasing Munch's unique printmaking methods that enhance its artistic relevance.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Indiana mother wins appeal, avoids college costs after son ignored 25 texts over four years
item.description: An Indiana appeals court has determined that a mother is not obliged to finance her son's tertiary education, citing four years of estrangement post-family split as decisive. The ruling highlighted that the son's voluntary disengagement from their relationship granted the mother a valid legal defense. Furthermore, the court dismissed the father's appeal as insufficient to impact the prior court's conclusions, reaffirming existing Indiana law on parental responsibilities regarding education.

item.title: US charges 48 non-citizens in election-related cases across five states; two Indians named
item.description: The US Justice Department has announced charges against 48 non-citizens in election-related cases across Pennsylvania, California, Florida, New York and Nevada. Two Indian nationals are among those accused. The cases involve allegations of illegal voting in federal elections, fraudulent voter registration and false claims of US citizenship, including alleged misrepresentations in naturalisation proceedings. All defendants are presumed innocent.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Maine woman wins federal court battle over faulty $189,471 foreclosure notice
item.description: In a landmark decision, a federal court upheld that Maine's foreclosure notification regulations extend protections to non-borrowing spouses. This case highlighted a scenario where a woman faced foreclosure due to her husband's refinancing actions, taken without her consent. The lender's notice was found lacking in clarity regarding amounts owed, underscoring the critical need for adherence to state laws which safeguard homeowners from improper foreclosure practices.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk
